exercises.title: 10m Air Pistol Exercise
exercises.text:
This exercise is designed to shoot air pistols so that the participant can endeavour to achieve the best and most consistent accuracy. The shooter shoots in the traditional manner from the prone position, from the bench or with "crossed sticks" or with a single support of a similar design.
 FIREARMS PERMITTED: Only Springer, CO2, or PCP Air Pistols in the following Calibres may be used (.177 / 4.5mm ; .20 / 5mm ; .22 / 5,58mm ; .25 / 6,35mm)
 SHOOTING DISTANCE: The shooting distance measured from the target to the edge of the firing line closest to the shooter is 10 meters.
 COURSE OF FIRE: Two shots per small target printed on one A4 page shot at 10m with score counting out of 100points
 FIRING POSITION: Standing position, Air Pistol held in one or both hands, with all portions of the shooter`s clothing, body and firearm clear of artificial support.

exercises.title: .22 Rimfire Semi-Auto Pistol Exercises (Precision Shooting)
exercises.text:
5m, .22 Rimfire Derringer & Vest Gun Exercise - Exercise Rules 
A .22 Rimfire Derringer & Vest-Gun is a handgun of which the barrel is not longer than 3 inches and of which the whole frame, sights and grip, fits into a rectangle of 130mm x 100mm.
The Rimfire Derringer & Vest-Gun must fit into the box described on the page you can Download HERE 
 FIREARMS PERMITTED: .22 Rimfire Derringers and .22 Rimfire calibre Vest-Guns (.22S, .22LR, .22Mag) and .22wmr calibre revolvers (all types of sight configuration allowed)
 SHOOTING DISTANCE: The shooting distance measured from the target to the front edge of the Shooter's firing line is 5 metres.
 COURSE OF FIRE: Total of 5 shots at 5m – shot on your own time, on one target and scored out of 50 points.
 FIRING POSITION: Standing position, Derringer or Vest-Gun held in one or both hands, with all portions of the shooter`s clothing, body and firearm clear of artificial support.

exercises.title: 20m, Single Shot Sporting Handgun Exercise
exercises.text:
This exercise is designed to shoot air rifles for the participant to achieve best and most consistent accuracy. The shooter shoots in the traditional manner from the prone position to the bench or with ‘crossed sticks’ or a single support of a similar manner.
 FIREARMS PERMITTED: Only Springer, CO2, or PCP Air Rifles in the following Calibres may be used (.177 / 4.5mm ; .20 / 5mm ; .22 / 5,5mm ; .25 / 6,35mm)
 SHOOTING DISTANCE: The shooting distance measured from the target to the edge of the firing line closest to the shooter is 25 metres.
 COURSE OF FIRE: Strictly two shots on each of the 5 smaller circles on the A4 Target, shot @ 25m on your own time, and scored out of 100 points.
 FIRING POSITION: Any shooting position is valid, with the exception that the butt of the gunstock may not be rested or supported on anything else than being in the shoulder.

exercises.title: Handgun Rapid Fire Exercises (Rapid Fire Shooting)
10m, .22 Rimfire Pistol Rapid Fire Exercise
10m, Centre-Fire Rapid Fire Pistol Exercise
10m, Centre-Fire Rapid Fire Revolver Exercise
exercises.text:
FIREARMS PERMITTED:   Revolvers in centre-fire calibres from .38 Special and Larger
 SHOOTING DISTANCE:   The shooting distance measured from the target to the edge of the firing line closest to the shooter is 10 meters.
 COURSES OF FIRE:    The exercise consists of firing two strings of 5 shots in 30 seconds at 10 metres on the same prescribed NHSA A4 target, with manually reloading of revolver in between shooting of two strings to score 100 points
 DOUBLE OR SINGLE ACTION REVOLVERS :   no optical sights allowed – maximum barrel length 4,2 inches / 100mm:
–        Load 5 rounds in cylinder;
–        De-cock revolver and place empty cylinder under hammer (hammer down)
–        On start signal, fire first string of 5 shots at prescribed target @ 10 metres;
–        Manually load next 5 rounds in cylinder and fire second string of 5 shots at same prescribed target @ 10 metres;
 Note:   Time for exercise to be completed is 30 seconds – speed loaders may be used – or a maximum of 5 rounds may be manually loaded at a time. 
Timing starts when time keeper gives the command Start (Fire) and ends when the last shot has been fired.
 FIRING POSITION:   Standing position, handgun held in one or both hands, with all portions of the shooter`s clothing, body and firearm clear of artificial support

exercises.title: 20m, Handgun Steel Plate Exercise (Pistols & Revolvers)
exercises.text:
It is compulsory that a video of the exercise being shot shall be made for ratification if need arises. The video must be taken from behind the shooter in such a manner that the shooting position of the shooter is visible in relationship to the Steel Plates being shot at.
 FIREARMS PERMITTED:   All Calibres and all actions of Handguns allowed.
 SHOOTING DISTANCE:   The shooting distance measured from the target to the front edge of the Shooter's firing line is 20 metres.
 COURSES OF FIRE:  Stationary Falling Plate Exercise: 5 shots at 20m on your own time, shot on 5 individual falling steel plates set-up next to one another, and scored out of 50 points
 SCORING:  10 points per dropped plate and 5 points per hit steel plate which did not fall over and 0 points per missed steel plate. 
Plates to be spaced with at least 200mm gap between them, and set up on a flat / horizontal surface.
 FIRING POSITION:  Any firing positions allowed 
 TARGETS:  Shall be of square profile of maximum 300mm (w) x 300mm (h)  x 10mm thick (b), with a support base extending at least 50mm in font of upright of plate. 5% variation in any of above measurements are allowed.

exercises.title: 20m, Handgun Gong Exercise (Pistols & Revolvers)
exercises.text:
It is compulsory that a video of the exercise being shot shall be made for ratification if need arises. The video must be taken from behind the shooter in such a manner that the shooting position of the shooter is visible in relationship to Gong being shot at.
 FIREARMS PERMITTED:  All Calibres and Actions of Handguns Allowed
 SHOOTING DISTANCE:   The shooting distance measured from the target to the front edge of the Shooter's firing line is 20 metres.
 COURSES OF FIRE – Gong Exercise:   5 shots at 20m on one gong on your own time, shot on one swinging gong (or multiple swinging gongs) and scored out of 50 points – 10 points per hit and 0 points per missed shot (gong).
 FIRING POSITION:   Any firing positions allowed
 TARGETS:  Gongs:  shall be of round profile with a maximum diameter of 300mm excluding the support brackets / chains etc. Smaller gongs may be used, but no adjustment in scoring or distance are allowed.

exercises.title: 15m, Black Powder Handgun Exercise
exercises.text:
FIREARMS PERMITTED:   Either flint lock or cap lock pistols as well as cap revolvers in only the following calibres: .32, .36, .44, .45, .50, & .57
Only cast lead bullets, with or without gas checks, may be used;
Either smokeless or black powder loads may be used;
Optical or metallic sights may be used (mark sight type on target).
 SHOOTING DISTANCE:   The shooting distance measured from the target to the front edge of the Shooter's firing line is 15 metres.
 COURSE OF FIRE:   5 shots at 15m shot on the relevant A4 NSA Black Powder Handgun Target, in your own time scored out of 50 points.
 FIRING POSITION:   Free style (out of hand) standing, kneeling, sitting or prone position with no additional support whatsoever (i.e. bag) for handgun.  Shooter`s elbows may rest on ground, on knees or on bench-top

exercises.title: 50m, Historic Rife Exercise
exercises.text:
This exercise is designed to shoot historic centre-fire rifles for the participant to achieve the best and most consistent accuracy.  The shooter shoots in the traditional manner from the prone position, from the bench or with "crossed sticks" or with a single support of a similar design.
 HISTORIC RIFLES 
Any centre-fire calibre of which the specific rifle with which the target is shot, is manufactured before 1950, or is a proven centre-fire military bolt action rifle, or falling block or with lever action, which could have been manufactured after 1950, but excludes all specific sniper rifles manufactured after 1950.
Any centre-fire calibre of any rifle design (pre-1900 reproduction) with an external hammer is also allowed, if build to pre-1900 specification and fitted with correct period metallic sights.
 Only open metallic sights are allowed. 
 THE EXERCISE 
 FIREARMS ALLOWED:   
Any centre-fire calibre of which the specific rifle with which the target is shot, is proven to be produced before 1950 (proof of year of production of rifle must  accompany all shot target scores logged on your personal Natshoot web page).
Any centre-fire calibre of any rifle design (pre-1900 reproduction) with an external hammer is allowed, if build to pre-1900 specification and fitted with correct period metallic sights.
Any centre-fire calibre bolt action military rifle
Only open sights are allowed.
 SHOOTING DISTANCE:   The shooting distance measured from the target to the edge of the firing line closest to the shooter is 50 metres.
 COURSE OF FIRE:    3 shots at 50m shot on one A4 target in your own time scored out of 30 points.
 FIRING POSITION:   Any shooting position is valid; rifles may be rested on a bench, with the exception that rifle rests of which the front and the back are connected by a centre piece, may not be used.

exercises.title: .22 Semi-Auto Rapid Fire Rifle Exercise (Rapid Fire Shooting)
exercises.text:
.22 Semi-Auto Rimfire Rifle Exercise - Exercise Rules 
It is compulsory that a video of the exercise being shot shall be made for ratification if need arises. The video must be taken from behind the shooter in such a manner that the shooting position of the shooter is visible in relationship to target A and target B. The video must also capture the shooting time used for both targets of this exercise.
 FIREARMS ALLOWED:   Only .22 Rimfire Calibre in Semi-Auto Rifles or in Pistol Carbine Conversion Kits (i.e. 22LR Rimfire) 
Exercise shot on two Targets against time
 A-Target  – Rapid fire: Firing of 10 shots at  25 metres  – timed string (no time limits)  
 B-Target  – Rapid fire: Firing of 10 shots at  25 metres  – timed string (no time limits)      
 SCORING: 
Participants must shoot 10 shots at each target
Shots count according to the number of the scoring ring they are fired into.  Cut shots counts the higher number – a cut shot is a shot of which the hole of the shot (not its leaded edge) cuts the outside line of any scoring ring
 TIME PENALTIES:  All shots outside of scoring rings but still on the edge of the paper the target is printed upon, or which are totally off the target (A or B), represents a time penalty of + 3,00 seconds / per shot for that specific target.
 Scoring the A-Target:   Score is calculated as the number of points scored with the 10 shot string – that total is then divided by the number of seconds (two decimals) it took to shoot the 10 shots (Original time plus time penalties) = the Mark for the A-Target (i.e. 70 points divided by 30,00 seconds = a Mark of 2,33)
 Scoring the B-Target:   Score is calculated as the number of points scored with the 10 shot string – that total is then divided by the number of seconds (two decimals) it took to shoot the 10 shots (Original time plus time penalties) = the Mark for the A-Target (i.e. 70 points divided by 22,00 seconds = a Mark of 3,18)
 Example of scoring:  Mark for A-Target is 2,33 + Mark for B-Target is 3,18 – add Mark for A-Target and Mark for B-Target =  Ex ercise Mark of 5,52 
The score achieved for each Target is entered onto the Score Sheet, which must accompany the Targets at submission of scores on the participant`s Personal Natshoot Profile Page.
___________________
 TIME KEEPING:   Time keeping may be done with a stopwatch and by any person who is able and willing to assist members with the exercise and who signs the targets and the score sheet on the relevant space provided with inclusion of his/her ID number and cell phone number.
Timing starts when time keeper says Start (fire) and ends when the last shot has been fired.
___________________
 SIGHT CONFIGURATION:   Any sight configuration may be used (open iron sights or any optical or laser sight).
___________________
 FIRING POSITIONS:   The standing position without support is mandatory for whole exercise – gun strap may be used.

It is compulsory that a video of the exercise being shot shall be made for ratification if need arises. The video must be taken from behind the shooter in such a manner that the shooting position of the shooter is visible in relationship to target A and target B. The video must also capture the shooting time used for both targets of this exercise.
 FIREARMS ALLOWED:   Only Centre-fire Semi-auto Rifle/Carbines FROM AND ABOVE the so-called .30 calibres (i.e. .300 Win. Mag., .300 WSM, 7.62 x 39mm, .308 Win. = 7.62x51mm, .30/06, .35 Whelen)
Exercise shot on two Targets against time
 A-Target  – Rapid fire: 10 shots at  25 metres  – timed string (no time limits)  
B-Target – Rapid fire: 10 shots at  50 metres  – timed string (no time limits)      
 SCORING: 
Participants must shoot 10 shots at each target
Shots count according to the number of the scoring ring they are fired into.  Cut shots counts the higher number – a cut shot is a shot of which the hole of the shot (not its leaded edge) cuts the outside line of any scoring ring
 TIME PENALTIES:   All shots outside of scoring rings but still on the edge of the paper the target is printed upon, or which are totally off the target (A or B), represents a time penalty of + 3,00 seconds / per shot for that specific target. 
 Scoring the A-Target:   Score is calculated as the number of points scored with the 10 shot string – that total is then divided by the number of seconds (two decimals) it took to shoot the 10 shots (Original time plus time penalties) = the Mark for the A-Target (i.e. 70 points divided by 30,00 seconds = a Mark of 2,33)
 Scoring the B-Target:   Score is calculated as the number of points scored with the 10 shot string – that total is then divided by the number of seconds (two decimals) it took to shoot the 10 shots (Original time plus time penalties) = the Mark for the A-Target (i.e. 70 points divided by 22,00 seconds = a Mark of 3,18)
 Example of scoring:  Mark for A-Target is 2,33 + Mark for B-Target is 3,18 – add Mark for A-Target and Mark for B-Target =  Exercise Mark of 5,52 
The score achieved for each Target is entered onto the Score Sheet, which must accompany the Targets at submission of scores on the participant`s Personal Natshoot Profile Page.
___________________
 TIME KEEPING:   Time keeping may be done with a stopwatch and by any person who is able and willing to assist members with the exercise and who signs the targets and the score sheet on the relevant space provided with inclusion of his/her ID number and cell phone number.
Timing starts when time keeper says Start (fire) and ends when the last shot has been fired.
___________________
 SIGHT CONFIGURATION:   Any sight configuration may be used (open or scoped sights).
___________________
 FIRING POSITIONS:   The standing position is mandatory for all exercises – gun straps may be used.

exercises.title: Shotgun Clay Target Shooting
exercises.text:
FIREARMS ALLOWED: All double barrelled shotguns in bores (calibres) from 410, 12Ga, 16Ga, 18Ga, and 20Ga.
Semi-automatic and pump action shotguns allowed if ranges allow them – Single barrelled shotguns specific for ATA Trap are allowed where ranges allow such shotguns
 COURSES OF FIRE 
 COMPAK – Any Compak range set-up consisting of one round of, or multiples of rounds of, 25 clays.
 SKEET (NSSA Skeet)
All variants of Skeet consisting of one round of, or multiples of rounds of, 25 clays.
 ATA & Olympic TRAP 
All forms of Trap disciplines consisting of one round of, or multiples of rounds of, 25 clays.
 DTL Trap 
Consisting of one round of, or multiples of rounds of, 25 clays counting 75 points.
 SPORTING CLAYS (FITASC Sporting, English Sporting & English Doubles)
All variants of Sporting Clays consisting of one round of, or multiples of rounds of, 25 clays.
 UNIVERSAL TRENCH: All forms of Trench disciplines consisting of one round of, or multiples of rounds of, 25 clays.
 FIRING POSITION: It is NHSA policy that participants conform to standard acceptable shotgunning stances and that shotguns will be handled with the utmost of care and safety in mind – conform to range set standards at all times (eye and ear protection is mandatory).
 TARGETS: A normal round of any of the above mentioned clay target shooting disciplines, consisting of a combination of normal clays, midi clays, mini clays, super mini clays, battue clays, or rabbit clays (thrown with a hand trap or with an electric operated trap machine).
Skeet, (NSSA Skeet) (per round of 25 clays);
Sporting Clays (FITASC Sporting, English Sporting & English Doubles) (per round of 25 clays);
Trap (ATA Trap or DTL Trap & Olympic Trap) (per round of 25 clays), and;
Universal Trench (all formats of trench) (per round of 25 clays).

exercises.title: 20m All Action Shotguns Steel Plate Shooting Exercise
exercises.text:
FIREARMS PERMITTED:   All Action Shotguns in Bores 10Ga, 11Ga, 12Ga, 16Ga, 18Ga, 20Ga & 28Ga & 410 Calibre
 SHOT SIZE:  Strictly only #3 shot to #8 shot
 SHOOTING DISTANCE:   The shooting distance measured from the target to the edge of the firing line closest to the shooter is 20 metres.
 COURSES OF FIRE  (Stationary Falling Plate only):  
The exercise consists of firing 10 shots at 20m on 10 individual falling steel plates, set-up next to one another.
 SCORING:  Each of the 10 steel plates hit, scores 10 points – Each of the 10 steel plates missed, scores 0 points – Score for exercise is calculated out of 100 points.
 FIRING POSITION:   The standing position is mandatory – no gun-slings allowed.
 TARGETS:    Stationary Falling plates:  shall be of square profile of maximum 300m (w) x 300mm (h)  x 10mm thick (b), with a support base extending at least 50mm in font of upright of plate. 5% variation in any of above measurements are allowed.
It is compulsory that a video of the exercise being shot shall be made for ratification if need arises. The video must be taken from behind the shooter in such a manner that the shooting position of the shooter is visible in relationship to falling plates being shot at.

exercises.title: 20m All Action Shotguns Gong Shooting Exercise
exercises.text:
FIREARMS PERMITTED:   All Actions Shotguns in bores 110Ga, 11Ga, 12Ga, 16Ga, 18Ga, 20Ga, 28Ga & 410 calibre
 SHOT SIZE:  Strictly only #3 shot to #8 shot
 SHOOTING DISTANCE:   The shooting distance measured from the target to the edge of the firing line closest to the shooter is 20 metres.
 COURSES OF FIRE  (Hanging Gong only):  The exercise consists of firing 10 shots at 20m on 1 or more hanging gongs.
 SCORING:  Each Gong hit, scores 10 points – Each Gong missed, scores 0 points – Score for exercise is calculated out of 100 points.
 FIRING POSITION:   The standing position is mandatory – no gun-slings allowed.
 TIME LIMIT:    The exercise must be completed in 60 seconds
 TARGETS:  Hanging Gongs:  shall be of round profile with a maximum diameter of 300mm excluding the support brackets / chains etc.  Smaller gongs may be used, but no adjustment in scoring or distance are allowed. 
It is compulsory that a video of the exercise being shot shall be made for ratification if need arises. The video must be taken from behind the shooter in such a manner that the shooting position of the shooter is visible in relationship to Gong being shot at.

exercises.title: 7m, Centre-Fire Carry Gun Exercise
exercises.text:
7m CENTRE-FIRE CARRY GUN EXERCISE 
 CARRY GUN: Centre-Fire Handguns of calibre 7,65mm and larger, fitting in a Box [rectangle] of 190mm [L] x 140mm [H] (all types of sight configuration allowed)
The Carry Gun must fit the Box described on the page you can Download HERE 
 SHOOTING DISTANCE: The shooting distance measured from the target to the front edge of the Shooter's firing line is 7 metres.
 COURSE OF FIRE: Total of 5 shots at 7m – shot on your own time, on one target and scored out of 50 points.
 FIRING POSITION: Standing position, Carry Gun held in one or both hands, with all portions of the shooter`s clothing, body and firearm clear of artificial support.
